skipped.Ampere (Altra, Altra Max, AmpereOne): Open Data has no Linux-aarch64 launcher and the full 2026-11-21 snapshot holds no Ampere, Altra, Neoverse or Linux-aarch64 entry. The Ampere Blender results that exist are Phoronix Test Suite runs (pts/blender, e.g. Blender 4.1 BMW27/Classroom/Fishy Cat/Barbershop render times in seconds on an Altra Max, OpenBenchmarking result 2205062-NE-BLENDER2555 and Phoronix reviews): a fixed-sample render time of different .blend files, with no clean conversion to Open Data samples per minute, and their power is CPU sensor or IPMI averages over a whole suite, not wall power for the render. Jeff Geerling's Thelio Astra issue (sbc-reviews #53) has one BMW27 time rendered on an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA, not on the Ampere CPU; his blog posts have no Blender numbers.
skipped.Snapdragon X Elite three-scene sum: already on the page (nv2.py, nv2_rows.json id 43); this step adds only its per-scene rows.
skipped.Snapdragon X Plus, X2 Elite, X2 Elite Ex: Open Data runs exist (Windows ARM64; the X2 chips mostly with Blender 5.1 and 5.2, not 4.5.0), but no machine with these chips has a wall-power reading on the page to borrow.
skipped.Notebookcheck Blender 3.3 Classroom CPU: a fixed-sample render of the classic Classroom demo in Blender 3.3, not the time-limited Open Data classroom scene in samples per minute; the page has no convention for it (cpubench.py leaves it out too).
skipped.Adreno GPU: Cycles has no Adreno backend (CUDA, OptiX, HIP, oneAPI and Metal only), so Open Data has no Snapdragon GPU runs; the matrix already marks that cell n/a.
